# One integer coordinate: an actual common H menu cannot span a source interval

This is an independent H-specific source-exclusion argument using the exact base-tilt quotas and affine envelope. The underlying adjacency phenomenon was already proved for ordinary depth in `candidate 9afb6a8708a420d7`; Optimal is extending that older endpoint-trimming proof directly to the concave H buffer. Thus the present theorem is an independent verification and frontier simplification, not a newly discovered ordinary n=1 adjacency theorem.

It supersedes the n=1 full-rank one-group filling program at actual small-epsilon H configurations: those occupied-source-interval hypotheses cannot occur. The conditional filling and strict-convex implications remain mathematically correct but have no such actual n=1 inputs.

## 1. Precise hypotheses

Let d>=1 and let C be a compact convex body in R x R^d. Its complete integer base P is finite; every sampled fiber used below is full-dimensional. Suppose there are distinct integer sources a<b, an affine map y(z), a positive affine function ell(z) on the entire base projection, and a d-dimensional convex body D with 0 interior such that

    K_z subset y(z)+ell(z)D for every real base z,
    K_z=y(z)+ell(z)D for z in [a,b].                 (1)

Endpoint equality alone would imply the interval equality by convexity and the envelope.

Suppose a finite menu of actual mass-Q buffered caps H_j is minimizing at EACH source (a,y(a)) and (b,y(b)), is proper on both source fibers, and propagates in pointed coordinates as

    H_j: u_j·xi+c_j>=0,
    xi=(x-y(z))/ell(z),                             (2)

where every u_j is nonzero. Assume there are positive weights rho_j with sum one such that

    sum_j rho_j (u_j·xi+c_j)>0 for every xi in D.     (3)

For the actual single H group, c_j=epsilon f_D Gamma(u_j), and its contact equation makes (3) equal to epsilon f_D P_D(xi)>0. Thus this is the SAME physical menu, with no changed cap weights or supporting allocations.

**Theorem.** Hypotheses (1)--(3) are impossible. In particular an actual H group in one integer dimension cannot have a full-rank occupied source interval (whose integer width is at least two).

## 2. Exact pure-base tilt quota

Fix one selected cap. Denote its total proper-section coareas by S_z, its outside-supporting facet coareas by A_z, and its inside-supporting facet coareas by B_z. All are divided by the common |u|. For d=1 these are endpoint counting coareas. Strictly empty/full fibers and lower-dimensional exposed faces contribute zero.

At a source p, changing only the base normal coefficient by t v changes the buffered threshold by t v p and the fiber margin by t v(z-p). The buffer and the continuous normal remain fixed. Direct one-sided slicing gives the exact right derivative

    D_p(v)=sum_proper S_z v(z-p)
       +sum_outside A_z[v(z-p)]_+
       +sum_inside B_z[v(z-p)]_-,                   (4)

where r_-=min(r,0). Actual cap minimality gives D_p(v)>=0. Add the inequalities p=a,v=-1 and p=b,v=+1. With m=b-a>=1,

    m sum_proper S_z
      +sum_inside B_z[(z-a)_+ +(b-z)_+]
    <=sum_outside A_z[(a-z)_+ +(z-b)_+].            (5)

This is the independently audited quota of `candidate bd07538e1a7bbdd9`. There is no epsilon error, and inside support only increases the left side. Since source traces are proper, its left side is positive. Each selected cap therefore has an outside-supporting fiber strictly to the left of a or strictly to the right of b.

For one cap there is at most one outside-supporting fiber on each side. For example, if L_1<L_2<a were two such fibers, interpolate a point on the cap plane at L_1 with a cap-interior point at source a. At base L_2 this gives a point strictly inside the cap, contradicting outside support there. The same argument applies on the right. The outside facet with positive coarea needed in (5) is consequently unique on its side.

## 3. One selected cap has no right outside support

For each xi in D, the set of real bases for which

    (z,y(z)+ell(z)xi) belongs to C

is an interval containing [a,b]. This uses the affine physical map in z. Therefore pointed fibers D_z=(K_z-y(z))/ell(z) are nested decreasing along each side away from [a,b].

If cap j has an outside support at some sampled z_j>b, every farther-right pointed fiber lies in its closed complement. If this occurred for every selected cap, the last positive sampled fiber would lie in their common closed complement. That contradicts (3). Thus one selected cap has NO right outside support. By (5) it has a left outside facet at a unique integer L<a, with A_L>0.

Reflecting the same argument shows that some selected cap has no left outside support and has a right outside facet. These statements do not presume that every cap has both types.

## 4. Choose the side where the affine scale increases toward the sources

First suppose ell is nondecreasing. Choose the cap from Section 3 with only a left outside facet L<a. Write h=b-L, so h>m. Let

    s_D=H_(d-1)(D intersect {u·xi+c=0})/|u|>0.

Its source section at b has coarea

    S_b=ell(b)^(d-1) s_D,

while its outside facet is a subset of the same pointed section and has

    A_L<=ell(L)^(d-1) s_D.                          (6)

Every real base L<z<=b has a proper trace. For z<b, a cap-plane point in K_L combined with a cap-interior point and own ball in K_b produces points strictly above the cap plane in K_z. Points strictly below it follow by combining an interior point of the full-dimensional outside body K_L with a below-plane point in the proper body K_b. The source at b is proper by hypothesis. In particular ALL h integer bases L+1,...,b give proper sections.

For d>=2, align the affine fiber cap planes by an affine translation into the fixed continuous subspace u-perp. The resulting (d-1)-dimensional sections form an actual convex family. Brunn--Minkowski, with theta=(z-L)/(b-L), gives

    S_z^(1/(d-1))
      >=(1-theta)A_L^(1/(d-1))+theta S_b^(1/(d-1)).

Using (6) and affine ell,

    S_z >= A_L[ell(z)/ell(L)]^(d-1) >= A_L,
                       L<z<=b.                     (7)

All coarea factors |u| are common and cancel before this power calculation. The final inequality uses precisely the chosen monotone side.

For d=1, every proper section and the outside endpoint have the same counting coarea 1/|u|, so S_z=A_L directly; no undefined exponent 1/(d-1) is used.

## 5. The integer quota contradicts section convexity

The selected cap has no right outside facet and its left one is unique. Dropping the nonnegative inside penalty from (5), then using all h proper integer sections in (7), gives

    m h A_L <= m sum_proper S_z
             <= A_L(a-L)=A_L(h-m).

Since A_L>0, this says m h<=h-m. But m is a positive integer, so m h>=h>h-m. This is a contradiction.

If ell is nonincreasing, reflect the integer coordinate z -> -z and use the selected cap with only a right outside facet. Reflection preserves the integer lattice, cap minimality and all coareas, and makes ell nondecreasing in the reflected coordinate. The same contradiction follows. Constant ell is included in either case.

Thus the theorem holds for every d>=1, with the actual finite epsilon, all oblique caps, all supporting incidences, and no limiting selector argument.

## 6. Consequence and limits

At an actual one-integer H configuration with a full-rank occupied deepest hull, the proved cover construction would supply exactly the envelope and propagated common menu above. It therefore cannot occur. The resulting isolated/adjacent-source cases still have one or two vertex groups, and this argument gives no Gamma_d/2 payment for their outside-source target fibers. Nor does one-dimensional nesting extend to arbitrary base directions in n>=2. General lower-rank or hollow source groups remain genuine obligations.
